notes: Celgene paid ~$7.2B for Receptos, whose lead asset ozanimod is an oral, selective sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator developed for both ulcerative colitis and relapsing multiple sclerosis. Ozanimod was in Phase 3 at deal time and later won FDA approval as Zeposia (MS 2020, UC 2021). Peak-sales figure of $1.8B is a sell-side ESTIMATE reflecting consensus across the MS + UC indications at the time of the deal — not a Celgene-disclosed number. EV/peak of ~4.0x reflects a de-risked oral S1P modulator with dual large-indication optionality.
selection_rationale: Oral S1P modulator autoimmune small-molecule M&A with public deal terms — same mechanistic class as etrasimod (Arena), giving the autoimmune · small_molecule cohort a coherent S1P-modulator core plus the oral BTK (Principia) data point.
source: Celgene/Receptos press release Jul 14 2015; Receptos SEC filings; FDA Zeposia approvals 2020-2021. Peak-sales is a sell-side consensus ESTIMATE (not company-disclosed).
